Operational Data Analyst
Location: Normanton. Department: Operations. Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience.
About the role
Generator Power is looking for an analytical and organised Operational Data Analyst to join the Operations team at Normanton. You will own the daily and weekly operational reporting cycle, producing accurate and timely analysis across breakdowns, faults, deployments, permits, fuel usage and telemetry. Working closely with the Operational Analytics Manager and operational teams, you will maintain reliable datasets, identify trends and exceptions, and turn complex information into clear reports.
Key responsibilities
• Produce and distribute daily breakdown and fault analysis across Telecoms, Utilities and General Operations.
• Prepare the daily Telecoms fault report for the 9:00am operational call (outstanding faults, ageing cases, repeat failures).
• Maintain operational datasets covering jobs, deployments, services, refuels, invoices and asset status.
• Check and validate information from operational systems, investigating missing or conflicting data.
• Produce weekly customer reporting packs (reliability, fuel usage, site access efficiencies).
• Monitor KPIs: fault volumes, response times, SLA performance, asset utilisation, deployment activity, fuel status, telemetry availability.
• Produce Excel reports, charts and commentary for depot teams, managers, directors and customers.
• Develop and improve reporting processes using Excel, Power Query, SQL, Power BI and Microsoft 365 tools.
• Maintain reporting records (data sources, calculation methods, procedures).
• Support monthly operational reviews, quarterly customer reviews, service-credit calculations and ad-hoc analysis.
Essential
• Strong working knowledge of Excel (formulas, lookups, PivotTables, charts, conditional formatting).
• Good numerical ability and confidence checking and explaining data.
• Strong written and verbal communication.
• Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach; able to manage multiple priorities.
• Practical experience analysing, checking or presenting data (employment, university projects, placements or internships).
• Ability to identify data-quality issues and investigate discrepancies.
• Confidence working independently while knowing when to escalate.
Desirable
• Power Query, Power BI, SQL or Power Automate.
• A degree in Data Analysis, Business, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, Engineering or another numerate subject.
• Experience in operational, service, logistics, engineering, utilities, telecoms, fleet, plant hire or asset-based environments.
• Exposure to KPI, SLA, fault, permit, fuel, telemetry or asset-utilisation reporting.
• Experience improving reporting processes or reducing manual data handling.

Junior Systems & Business Analyst
Norwich City Services Limited (NCSL) delivers and maintains Norwich's streets, parks and properties through its environmental and building repairs teams, employing over 300 people locally. Permanent role.
About the role
Support the maintenance, improvement and optimisation of operational systems, reporting and business processes. Working with operational teams, managers and system providers, you will help ensure system changes are implemented effectively, business requirements are understood, and management information stays accurate.
• Assist with system administration, upgrades, testing and user acceptance activities.
• Maintain system documentation, process maps and user guides.
• Analyse business processes, identify improvements, support service reviews, improvement projects and business cases.
• Produce operational and performance reports; develop management information and dashboards.
• Validate data quality and investigate inconsistencies; give insight on performance, productivity and customer outcomes.
• Act as a point of contact for system queries; support users with training and guidance; help deliver digital transformation.
• Workforce management and scheduling platforms such as Totalmobile are advantageous, not essential.
About you
• Highly organised and analytical with strong problem-solving and attention to detail.
• Experience working with data and Microsoft Excel; able to interpret and communicate findings clearly.
• Comfortable documenting processes and requirements and managing competing priorities.
• Genuine interest in systems, business improvement and data-driven decisions.
• Power BI, process mapping, CRM or scheduling systems advantageous; training and development provided.
• Collaborative, customer-focused and willing to learn new systems.
Benefits: Living Wage employer, cycle to work, employee assistance, 25 days' leave rising to 30 plus bank holidays and a Christmas shutdown. 37 hours a week; part time or job share considered.
Closing date: Monday 23 November 2026 (may close early). Pay: £28,924-£30,473 a year. In person.

GreenSquareAccord is investing in transformation, systems and service delivery, and is looking for an experienced Business Analyst to join the Strategic Delivery and Change team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, working across projects supporting business transformation, new system implementations and operational improvements.
The role
Reporting to the Senior Project and Change Manager, you will combine business-as-usual activity and project work across Finance and the wider organisation: gathering and documenting requirements, mapping current and future processes, facilitating workshops and working with stakeholders. • Lead workshops and stakeholder discussions on requirements, processes and improvements.

• Gather, analyse and document business requirements, including user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Work with Project Managers, the Data Migration Lead and project teams.

• Contribute to testing frameworks so requirements translate into effective testing.
• Maintain process maps, documentation and BA artefacts.
• Build relationships with stakeholders across departments.
About you (ideally)
• Previous experience in a Business Analyst role supporting projects and change.
• Strong AS-IS and TO-BE process mapping.
• Proven experience gathering, documenting and managing requirements.
• Writing user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Confidence facilitating workshops and engaging stakeholders at different levels.
• Supporting systems implementation, transformation or improvement projects.
• Understanding of testing frameworks.
• Strong communication, analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Visio or similar is beneficial; housing, local authority or public-sector experience advantageous but not essential.

• £46,000-£50,200 depending on experience; 12-month fixed-term contract; hybrid with one day a week in the Birmingham office.

Job summary
Support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management, performing data analysis and maintaining departmental statistics and reports used by leadership and management.

• Monitor monthly budget variance; year-end budget versus spend reconciliation with the general ledger.

• Monitor medicine purchasing, supplier pricing, inventory and stock turnover to cut cost and waste.
• Analyse expenditure and budgets against targets; evaluate Pharmacy First, vaccination and travel health services.
• Maintain pharmacy databases; support compliance with NHS reporting, UK GDPR and information governance.
Qualifications
• Bachelor degree in IT, Business Management, Finance, Accounting or Hospital Administration, or equivalent.
• Strong analytical skills.
• Two years' professional experience in healthcare (preferably pharmacy).
• Direct experience in data analysis and/or healthcare planning preferred.
Job types: Full-time, Permanent. Pay: £15.00-£18.00 per hour. Work location: in person.
